text:
reading war and peace every year sounds insane until you've read it

then you go read about napoleon/1812, u come back and u read it a 2nd time....gets 50% better

3rd time, u can study tolstoy first to enjoy it more, but by this point u just see why its the #1 novel of all time

stumbling onto random sentences or paragraphs with more value than entire books, u organically unlock more as u age

meanwhile moby dick I couldnt wait to finish and never reread again. half the fuckin book is whale science

anyone who claims they enjoy rereading those chapters =🧢

so unless this is a secret ball knower "re-read" where ur actually just reading some 150 pages -- and there def are 150 great ones in there -- this still isnt real

"yea it's a top 10 book if you skip 450 of the 600 pages"

excuse me

"yea he made 400 pages super boring so that u feel like ur lost at sea"

what the fuck are u talking about

most books are pretty good if u pretend the 500 worst pages dont exist

bunch of apology-laden gibberish

"ya this book seems like a winner, u know what could really push it over the top though, is to add the most boring 450 page whale encyclopedia u can find"

cope

the worst 150 pages from war and peace are better than anything from this excuse-ridden "if I had wheels I'd be a wagon"-ass novel

ex-whale re-reads, ex-boring pages

non-GAAP ass book reviews and shit...don't besmirch tolstoy's name again with these fugazi whale hijinks.

prob one of my favorite passages ever

Tolstoy describing Bezukhov's quest for "harmony within himself," in Book 13 of War and Peace

all the paths we saw him try, which failed...

only for him find peace where its always found -- in hardship, and in transcendence thru suffering. https://t.co/QvICvanSU1
